method: Reread complete revised items including metadata, references, key, every option and rationale against the original issue. Each row reflects actual independent reasoning, not automatic acceptance of proposed edits.
limitations: Not external clinician or psychometric validation
Primary-source checks are targeted and documented in prior reports; additional references supplied by the author are not claimed as newly independently verified.

items.assessment: Substance-specific assessment now competes with reasonable nutrition supports, while the reported clay and ice craving justify more than generic teaching.

Actual herbal use, prior gestational diabetes and low-mood impact give the prenatal preparation choices specific clinical relevance.

Stable parent and infant support obtaining medicine-specific advice before changing treatment or feeding; alternatives are plausible but premature.

issues: The clinically concerning sleep pattern is correct, but deferring a diary until the next annual visit retains an implausibly long delay foil.
